title: Normally open and normally closed contacts
summary: A normally open (NO) contact closes when actuated; a normally closed (NC) contact opens when actuated. Stop buttons and safety-related signals use NC contacts so that a broken wire is noticed.

sections.heading: Definitions
sections.body:
- **Normally open (NO)**: open at rest, closed while actuated. A Start button is usually NO: the PLC input is TRUE only while it is pressed.
- **Normally closed (NC)**: closed at rest, open while actuated. A Stop button is usually NC: the PLC input is TRUE while the button is **not** pressed.

sections.heading: Why Stop uses NC
sections.body: If the wire to an NC Stop button breaks, the input drops to FALSE exactly as if Stop were pressed, so the machine stops. With an NO Stop button a broken wire would go unnoticed until someone needs to stop the machine. This principle is called **fail-safe** or **wire-break safe** signalling.

sections.heading: Program consequences
sections.body:
For an NC Stop button the program uses the input directly in the run condition:

```
MotorContactor := (StartPB OR MotorContactor) AND StopPB;
```

Writing `NOT StopPB` is a classic mistake: the motor then only runs while Stop is held down. When a contact block is replaced by the wrong type during maintenance, the input logic inverts and the machine behaves strangely although the program never changed.
